name: Parallel Volume Rendering via k-d Tree Subdivision and Binary-Swap Compositing
aliases: Parallel volume rendering via k-d tree subdivision
definition: A parallel rendering technique for large volumetric datasets on a PC cluster that subdivides the volume spatially using a k-d tree, distributes subvolumes to nodes with limited video memory, and composites results using binary-swap compositing to avoid bandwidth bottlenecks.
summary: This method renders large volumes on clusters by using k-d trees to fit subvolumes in local memory and binary-swap compositing to minimize network contention.
